 * cost that grows with board size) and (b) snapshot accumulation: the tick
 * already probes the previous state file on the factory-data branch for the
 * publish sha; reusing that one fetch, every new snapshot carries forward
 * the timestamps it stamped before and stamps `now` on transitions it
 * witnesses (label present now, absent in the previous snapshot). (b) costs
 * ONE extra gh call per tick regardless of board size and is exact to the
 * tick cadence (~10 min) — chosen. Cost: the very first snapshot after the
 * upgrade has no label history (those fields stay null until each card's
 * next transition); GitHub-native fields (prCreated/mergedAt) are exact
 * from snapshot one. Snapshot history (the `<base>-history.json` index)
 * keeps the raw evidence for time travel either way.
 *
 * Pure functions here (no tool globals) — smAgent wires deps; tests inject
 * mocks. CommonJS module like every other js/ module.

 * ── Schema 2 (lifecycle timestamps) ──────────────────────────────────────────
 * Schema 1 carried only the label lanes — the board could see WHERE a card
 * was, never HOW LONG it had been there or when it moved. Schema 2 stamps
 * every card with the pipeline's transition times so the whole flow (dev →
 * PR → review → approve → validate → merge) is measurable:
 *
 *   prCreated     GitHub PR.created_at (github_list_prs — free, exact)
 *   mergedAt      GitHub PR.merged_at (merged PRs, last 24h lane)
 *   reviewedAt    ai_pr_reviewed  label time
 *   approvedAt    pr_approved     label time
 *   validatingAt  ai_validating   label time (the arm)
 *   devStartedAt  issue-side: first snapshot that saw agent:dev without
 *                 ai_developed (the dev leg's running window)
 *
 * Label times are NOT free GitHub fields. Two candidate sources were
 * prototyped: (a) per-item timeline REST calls (`issues/N/events` — one
 * request per PR per tick, 10-min cadence → rate-limit and wall-clock
 * cost that grows with board size) and (b) snapshot accumulation: the tick
 * already probes the previous state file on the factory-data branch for the
 * publish sha; reusing that one fetch, every new snapshot carries forward
 * the timestamps it stamped before and stamps `now` on transitions it
 * witnesses (label present now, absent in the previous snapshot). (b) costs
 * ONE extra gh call per tick regardless of board size and is exact to the
 * tick cadence (~10 min) — chosen. Cost: the very first snapshot after the
 * upgrade has no label history (those fields stay null until each card's
 * next transition); GitHub-native fields (prCreated/mergedAt) are exact
 * from snapshot one. Snapshot history (the `<base>-history.json` index)
 * keeps the raw evidence for time travel either way.
 *
 * Pure functions here (no tool globals) — smAgent wires deps; tests inject
 * mocks. CommonJS module like every other js/ module.
 */

 * ── Schema 2 (lifecycle timestamps) ──────────────────────────────────────────
 * Schema 1 carried only the label lanes — the board could see WHERE a card
 * was, never HOW LONG it had been there or when it moved. Schema 2 stamps
 * every card with the pipeline's transition times so the whole flow (dev →
 * PR → review → approve → validate → merge) is measurable:
 *
 *   prCreated     GitHub PR.created_at (github_list_prs — free, exact)
 *   mergedAt      GitHub PR.merged_at (merged PRs, last 24h lane)
 *   reviewedAt    ai_pr_reviewed  label time
 *   approvedAt    pr_approved     label time
 *   validatingAt  ai_validating   label time (the arm)
 *   devStartedAt  issue-side: first snapshot that saw agent:dev without
 *                 ai_developed (the dev leg's running window)
 *
 * Label times are NOT free GitHub fields. Two candidate sources were
 * prototyped: (a) per-item timeline REST calls (`issues/N/events` — one
 * request per PR per tick, 10-min cadence → rate-limit and wall-clock
 * cost that grows with board size) and (b) snapshot accumulation: the tick
 * already probes the previous state file on the factory-data branch for the
 * publish sha; reusing that one fetch, every new snapshot carries forward
 * the timestamps it stamped before and stamps `now` on transitions it
 * witnesses (label present now, absent in the previous snapshot). (b) costs
 * ONE extra gh call per tick regardless of board size and is exact to the
 * tick cadence (~10 min) — chosen. Cost: the very first snapshot after the
 * upgrade has no label history (those fields stay null until each card's
 * next transition); GitHub-native fields (prCreated/mergedAt) are exact
 * from snapshot one. Snapshot history (the `<base>-history.json` index)
 * keeps the raw evidence for time travel either way.
 *
 * Pure functions here (no tool globals) — smAgent wires deps; tests inject
 * mocks. CommonJS module like every other js/ module.

 * Schema 1 carried only the label lanes — the board could see WHERE a card

 * every card with the pipeline's transition times so the whole flow (dev →
 * PR → review → approve → validate → merge) is measurable:
 *
 *   prCreated     GitHub PR.created_at (github_list_prs — free, exact)

 * cost that grows with board size) and (b) snapshot accumulation: the tick

 * publish sha; reusing that one fetch, every new snapshot carries forward
 * the timestamps it stamped before and stamps `now` on transitions it

 * tick cadence (~10 min) — chosen. Cost: the very first snapshot after the
 * upgrade has no label history (those fields stay null until each card's
 * next transition); GitHub-native fields (prCreated/mergedAt) are exact
 * from snapshot one. Snapshot history (the `<base>-history.json` index)
 * keeps the raw evidence for time travel either way.
 *

 * keeps the raw evidence for time travel either way.

 *
 * ── Schema 2 (lifecycle timestamps) ──────────────────────────────────────────
 * Schema 1 carried only the label lanes — the board could see WHERE a card
 * was, never HOW LONG it had been there or when it moved. Schema 2 stamps
 * every card with the pipeline's transition times so the whole flow (dev →
 * PR → review → approve → validate → merge) is measurable:
 *
 *   prCreated     GitHub PR.created_at (github_list_prs — free, exact)
 *   mergedAt      GitHub PR.merged_at (merged PRs, last 24h lane)
 *   reviewedAt    ai_pr_reviewed  label time
 *   approvedAt    pr_approved     label time
 *   validatingAt  ai_validating   label time (the arm)
 *   devStartedAt  issue-side: first snapshot that saw agent:dev without
 *                 ai_developed (the dev leg's running window)
 *
 * Label times are NOT free GitHub fields. Two candidate sources were
 * prototyped: (a) per-item timeline REST calls (`issues/N/events` — one
 * request per PR per tick, 10-min cadence → rate-limit and wall-clock
 * cost that grows with board size) and (b) snapshot accumulation: the tick
 * already probes the previous state file on the factory-data branch for the
 * publish sha; reusing that one fetch, every new snapshot carries forward
 * the timestamps it stamped before and stamps `now` on transitions it
 * witnesses (label present now, absent in the previous snapshot). (b) costs
 * ONE extra gh call per tick regardless of board size and is exact to the
 * tick cadence (~10 min) — chosen. Cost: the very first snapshot after the
 * upgrade has no label history (those fields stay null until each card's
 * next transition); GitHub-native fields (prCreated/mergedAt) are exact
 * from snapshot one. Snapshot history (the `<base>-history.json` index)
 * keeps the raw evidence for time travel either way.
 *
 * Pure functions here (no tool globals) — smAgent wires deps; tests inject
 * mocks. CommonJS module like every other js/ module.
 */

 * Schema 1 carried only the label lanes — the board could see WHERE a card

 * every card with the pipeline's transition times so the whole flow (dev →
 * PR → review → approve → validate → merge) is measurable:
 *
 *   prCreated     GitHub PR.created_at (github_list_prs — free, exact)
 *   mergedAt      GitHub PR.merged_at (merged PRs, last 24h lane)
 *   reviewedAt    ai_pr_reviewed  label time

 *   devStartedAt  issue-side: first snapshot that saw agent:dev without

 * prototyped: (a) per-item timeline REST calls (`issues/N/events` — one

 * cost that grows with board size) and (b) snapshot accumulation: the tick
 * already probes the previous state file on the factory-data branch for the
 * publish sha; reusing that one fetch, every new snapshot carries forward
 * the timestamps it stamped before and stamps `now` on transitions it
 * witnesses (label present now, absent in the previous snapshot). (b) costs
 * ONE extra gh call per tick regardless of board size and is exact to the
 * tick cadence (~10 min) — chosen. Cost: the very first snapshot after the
 * upgrade has no label history (those fields stay null until each card's
 * next transition); GitHub-native fields (prCreated/mergedAt) are exact
 * from snapshot one. Snapshot history (the `<base>-history.json` index)
 * keeps the raw evidence for time travel either way.
 *
 * Pure functions here (no tool globals) — smAgent wires deps; tests inject
 * mocks. CommonJS module like every other js/ module.

 * ── Schema 2 (lifecycle timestamps) ──────────────────────────────────────────
 * Schema 1 carried only the label lanes — the board could see WHERE a card

 * every card with the pipeline's transition times so the whole flow (dev →
 * PR → review → approve → validate → merge) is measurable:
 *
 *   prCreated     GitHub PR.created_at (github_list_prs — free, exact)
 *   mergedAt      GitHub PR.merged_at (merged PRs, last 24h lane)
 *   reviewedAt    ai_pr_reviewed  label time
 *   approvedAt    pr_approved     label time
 *   validatingAt  ai_validating   label time (the arm)
 *   devStartedAt  issue-side: first snapshot that saw agent:dev without
 *                 ai_developed (the dev leg's running window)
 *
 * Label times are NOT free GitHub fields. Two candidate sources were
 * prototyped: (a) per-item timeline REST calls (`issues/N/events` — one
 * request per PR per tick, 10-min cadence → rate-limit and wall-clock
 * cost that grows with board size) and (b) snapshot accumulation: the tick
 * already probes the previous state file on the factory-data branch for the
 * publish sha; reusing that one fetch, every new snapshot carries forward
 * the timestamps it stamped before and stamps `now` on transitions it
 * witnesses (label present now, absent in the previous snapshot). (b) costs
 * ONE extra gh call per tick regardless of board size and is exact to the
 * tick cadence (~10 min) — chosen. Cost: the very first snapshot after the
 * upgrade has no label history (those fields stay null until each card's
 * next transition); GitHub-native fields (prCreated/mergedAt) are exact
 * from snapshot one. Snapshot history (the `<base>-history.json` index)
 * keeps the raw evidence for time travel either way.
 *
 * Pure functions here (no tool globals) — smAgent wires deps; tests inject
 * mocks. CommonJS module like every other js/ module.

 * ── Schema 2 (lifecycle timestamps) ──────────────────────────────────────────
 * Schema 1 carried only the label lanes — the board could see WHERE a card
 * was, never HOW LONG it had been there or when it moved. Schema 2 stamps
 * every card with the pipeline's transition times so the whole flow (dev →
 * PR → review → approve → validate → merge) is measurable:
 *
 *   prCreated     GitHub PR.created_at (github_list_prs — free, exact)
 *   mergedAt      GitHub PR.merged_at (merged PRs, last 24h lane)
 *   reviewedAt    ai_pr_reviewed  label time
 *   approvedAt    pr_approved     label time
 *   validatingAt  ai_validating   label time (the arm)
 *   devStartedAt  issue-side: first snapshot that saw agent:dev without
 *                 ai_developed (the dev leg's running window)
 *
 * Label times are NOT free GitHub fields. Two candidate sources were
 * prototyped: (a) per-item timeline REST calls (`issues/N/events` — one
 * request per PR per tick, 10-min cadence → rate-limit and wall-clock
 * cost that grows with board size) and (b) snapshot accumulation: the tick
 * already probes the previous state file on the factory-data branch for the
 * publish sha; reusing that one fetch, every new snapshot carries forward
 * the timestamps it stamped before and stamps `now` on transitions it
 * witnesses (label present now, absent in the previous snapshot). (b) costs
 * ONE extra gh call per tick regardless of board size and is exact to the
 * tick cadence (~10 min) — chosen. Cost: the very first snapshot after the
 * upgrade has no label history (those fields stay null until each card's
 * next transition); GitHub-native fields (prCreated/mergedAt) are exact
 * from snapshot one. Snapshot history (the `<base>-history.json` index)
 * keeps the raw evidence for time travel either way.
 *
 * Pure functions here (no tool globals) — smAgent wires deps; tests inject
 * mocks. CommonJS module like every other js/ module.

arguments.content:
## Issues/Notes

Rework for all 4 open review threads on gh-816 (1 BLOCKING, 1 IMPORTANT, 2 suggestions):

- 🚨 **Thread 1 (BLOCKING)** — the state-publish wiring forwarded only `jobParams.ciWorkflow`, dropping the documented `rule.ciWorkflow` precedence (honored by `dispatchCiWorkflow` and five sibling sites in the same function). Per-rule validation dispatches (multi-repo factory-sm, one `ci-workflow` input per rule) were misclassified as SM side-run legs: no discharge cite, dead `pr_validation` lane, no merged checks record.
- ⚠️ **Thread 2 (IMPORTANT)** — the fail-open classifier made *every* non-dispatch run a "real validation run"; an unrelated repo workflow (labeler/docs/lint) could steal the discharge cite from the machine's green validation or light `pr_validation` while nothing real was in flight.
- 💡 **Thread 3 (suggestion)** — a carried `merged_recent` checks record with an in-flight verdict would pin "validation in flight" on a merged card for the whole 24h window.
- 💡 **Thread 4 (suggestion)** — `auxiliary.state` introduced a third name for the value the cite already exposes as `verdict`/`conclusion`.

Threads 5–6 of the discussion dump are the review summary and the rework-armer notice (no `threadId`/inline anchor), so they are addressed here rather than as threaded replies: all three of their "Next Steps" items are implemented below.

## Approach

- **Thread 1 — precedence restored + pinned.** The wiring in `processRule` (js/smAgent.js) now resolves the knob through the same chain as its five siblings: `rule.ciWorkflow || ((RUN_JOB_PARAMS || {}).ciWorkflow) || 'quality.yml'`. A new e2e publish-tick test carries `rule.ciWorkflow: 'rulecheck.yml'` against `jobParamsPatch.ciWorkflow: 'wrong.yml'` — the rule's dispatch must be the cite, so if the jobParams knob ever won, every dispatch on the head would be a leg and the card would carry no cite at all.
- **Thread 2 — score-tier citing.** Classification untouched (fail-open stays: dynamic per-PR validation workflows have arbitrary paths, a path allowlist cannot express them); the *preference* is tightened in `headVerdict`. Real runs get a tier: **2** = the machine's own validation workflow (`.github/workflows/<ciWorkflow>` path match), **1** = every other real run. The best available tier cites; within the winning tier the newest terminal non-cancelled run decides (gh-191: cancelled never cites), else the newest active run. Effect: a `labeler` run finishing 20s after `quality.yml` can no longer steal the cite; an in-flight validation dispatch outranks a green unrelated run (so `pr_validation` lights on the real validation, never fronted by an unrelated green); an unrelated workflow only cites when nothing better exists. The residual breadth is now owned in the classifier comment (`event !== 'workflow_dispatch'` explicitly means "any repo workflow", not "validation").
- **Thread 3 — marked carried records.** When the merge tick must fall back to the previous snapshot's record, a **terminal** record carries as-is (resolved verdict, unmarked); a record whose conclusion never landed rides with `carried: true` so the board can render it unverified rather than live. A fresh cite from the runs list still wins over anything carried.
- **Thread 4 — one vocabulary.** `checks.auxiliary` is now built by the same `runCite()` as the cite (`verdict`/`conclusion`/`runId`/`name`/`sha`/`at`/`url`/`runStartedAt`/`updatedAt`) — the private `state` field is gone, and cite/auxiliary/carried records share one documented shape. The module-header schema note now documents the checks record family in full.

Schema-additive only (marker field + shape unification); the board reads `verdict`/`at` and tolerates extra keys. Cancelled runs remain never-a-verdict; a head with only side-run legs still shows no cite (the intended de-falsening).

## Files Modified

 * Schema 1 carried only the label lanes — the board could see WHERE a card

 * every card with the pipeline's transition times so the whole flow (dev →
 * PR → review → approve → validate → merge) is measurable:
 *
 *   prCreated     GitHub PR.created_at (github_list_prs — free, exact)
 *   mergedAt      GitHub PR.merged_at (merged PRs, last 24h lane)
 *   reviewedAt    ai_pr_reviewed  label time
 *   approvedAt    pr_approved     label time
 *   validatingAt  ai_validating   label time (the arm)
 *   devStartedAt  issue-side: first snapshot that saw agent:dev without
 *                 ai_developed (the dev leg's running window)
 *
 * Label times are NOT free GitHub fields. Two candidate sources were
 * prototyped: (a) per-item timeline REST calls (`issues/N/events` — one
 * request per PR per tick, 10-min cadence → rate-limit and wall-clock
 * cost that grows with board size) and (b) snapshot accumulation: the tick
 * already probes the previous state file on the factory-data branch for the
 * publish sha; reusing that one fetch, every new snapshot carries forward
 * the timestamps it stamped before and stamps `now` on transitions it
 * witnesses (label present now, absent in the previous snapshot). (b) costs
 * ONE extra gh call per tick regardless of board size and is exact to the
 * tick cadence (~10 min) — chosen. Cost: the very first snapshot after the
 * upgrade has no label history (those fields stay null until each card's
 * next transition); GitHub-native fields (prCreated/mergedAt) are exact
 * from snapshot one. Snapshot history (the `<base>-history.json` index)
 * keeps the raw evidence for time travel either way.
 *
 * Pure functions here (no tool globals) — smAgent wires deps; tests inject
 * mocks. CommonJS module like every other js/ module.

{"content":"## Issues/Notes

Rework for all 4 open review threads on gh-816 (1 BLOCKING, 1 IMPORTANT, 2 suggestions):

- 🚨 **Thread 1 (BLOCKING)** — the state-publish wiring forwarded only `jobParams.ciWorkflow`, dropping the documented `rule.ciWorkflow` precedence (honored by `dispatchCiWorkflow` and five sibling sites in the same function). Per-rule validation dispatches (multi-repo factory-sm, one `ci-workflow` input per rule) were misclassified as SM side-run legs: no discharge cite, dead `pr_validation` lane, no merged checks record.
- ⚠️ **Thread 2 (IMPORTANT)** — the fail-open classifier made *every* non-dispatch run a "real validation run"; an unrelated repo workflow (labeler/docs/lint) could steal the discharge cite from the machine's green validation or light `pr_validation` while nothing real was in flight.
- 💡 **Thread 3 (suggestion)** — a carried `merged_recent` checks record with an in-flight verdict would pin "validation in flight" on a merged card for the whole 24h window.
- 💡 **Thread 4 (suggestion)** — `auxiliary.state` introduced a third name for the value the cite already exposes as `verdict`/`conclusion`.

Threads 5–6 of the discussion dump are the review summary and the rework-armer notice (no `threadId`/inline anchor), so they are addressed here rather than as threaded replies: all three of their "Next Steps" items are implemented below.

## Approach

- **Thread 1 — precedence restored + pinned.** The wiring in `processRule` (js/smAgent.js) now resolves the knob through the same chain as its five siblings: `rule.ciWorkflow || ((RUN_JOB_PARAMS || {}).ciWorkflow) || 'quality.yml'`. A new e2e publish-tick test carries `rule.ciWorkflow: 'rulecheck.yml'` against `jobParamsPatch.ciWorkflow: 'wrong.yml'` — the rule's dispatch must be the cite, so if the jobParams knob ever won, every dispatch on the head would be a leg and the card would carry no cite at all.
- **Thread 2 — score-tier citing.** Classification untouched (fail-open stays: dynamic per-PR validation workflows have arbitrary paths, a path allowlist cannot express them); the *preference* is tightened in `headVerdict`. Real runs get a tier: **2** = the machine's own validation workflow (`.github/workflows/<ciWorkflow>` path match), **1** = every other real run. The best available tier cites; within the winning tier the newest terminal non-cancelled run decides (gh-191: cancelled never cites), else the newest active run. Effect: a `labeler` run finishing 20s after `quality.yml` can no longer steal the cite; an in-flight validation dispatch outranks a green unrelated run (so `pr_validation` lights on the real validation, never fronted by an unrelated green); an unrelated workflow only cites when nothing better exists. The residual breadth is now owned in the classifier comment (`event !== 'workflow_dispatch'` explicitly means "any repo workflow", not "validation").
- **Thread 3 — marked carried records.** When the merge tick must fall back to the previous snapshot's record, a **terminal** record carries as-is (resolved verdict, unmarked); a record whose conclusion never landed rides with `carried: true` so the board can render it unverified rather than live. A fresh cite from the runs list still wins over anything carried.
- **Thread 4 — one vocabulary.** `checks.auxiliary` is now built by the same `runCite()` as the cite (`verdict`/`conclusion`/`runId`/`name`/`sha`/`at`/`url`/`runStartedAt`/`updatedAt`) — the private `state` field is gone, and cite/auxiliary/carried records share one documented shape. The module-header schema note now documents the checks record family in full.

Schema-additive only (marker field + shape unification); the board reads `verdict`/`at` and tolerates extra keys. Cancelled runs remain never-a-verdict; a head with only side-run legs still shows no cite (the intended de-falsening).

## Files Modified

- `js/smAgent.js` — forward `rule.ciWorkflow` with the canonical precedence chain into `buildFactoryState` (gh-816 rework thread 1).
- `js/factoryState.js` — score-tier cite resolution in `headVerdict` (thread 2); `auxiliary` = `runCite(leg)` (thread 4); `carried: true` marker on non-terminal carried `merged_recent` records (thread 3); residual-risk note on the classifier; module-header schema note for the checks record family.
- `js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js` — 6 new tests (score beats recency, in-flight tier preference, documented fail-open residual, carried-marker cases), 5 existing expectations updated to the tightened spec, auxiliary vocabulary assertions.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` — `publishTick` gained a `rulePatch` opt (mirroring `jobParamsPatch`); new e2e rule-level precedence test; e2e auxiliary vocabulary assertions.

## Test Coverage

TDD throughout — every fix written RED first against the pre-fix code, then GREEN:

- **Thread 1**: `gh-816: rule-level ciWorkflow override reaches the snapshot builder (rule.ciWorkflow > jobParams.ciWorkflow)` — RED on the old wiring (cite resolved to the jobParams knob's run), proves the rule-level knob wins and the review leg stays auxiliary.
- **Thread 2**: `the validation workflow outranks a FRESHER unrelated repo workflow (score beats recency)` (RED: labeler stole the cite), `an in-flight validation dispatch outranks a green unrelated repo workflow (score tier first)` (RED), `an unrelated repo workflow still cites when nothing better exists (documented fail-open residual)` (pins the owned tradeoff), plus same-tier recency/truth tests retained.
- **Thread 3**: `a carried in-flight record rides the merged card marked carried (never reads live)` (RED: `carried` was `undefined`) + terminal-carried-unmarked assertion.
- **Thread 4**: auxiliary assertions in both suites (`verdict`/`conclusion` present, `state` gone).

Full suite after all fixes: **`run_all` 2204 passed / 0 failed** (incl. `run_factoryState` 100/0, `run_smAgent` 398/0, `run_reworkLatch` 31/0) — no regressions. All fixtures are generic (`acme/factory`, `o/r`, `labeler`/`rulecheck.yml`); no project-specific content introduced, per AGENTS.md.

 * ── Schema 2 (lifecycle timestamps) ──────────────────────────────────────────
 * Schema 1 carried only the label lanes — the board could see WHERE a card
 * was, never HOW LONG it had been there or when it moved. Schema 2 stamps
 * every card with the pipeline's transition times so the whole flow (dev →
 * PR → review → approve → validate → merge) is measurable:
 *
 *   prCreated     GitHub PR.created_at (github_list_prs — free, exact)
 *   mergedAt      GitHub PR.merged_at (merged PRs, last 24h lane)
 *   reviewedAt    ai_pr_reviewed  label time
 *   approvedAt    pr_approved     label time
 *   validatingAt  ai_validating   label time (the arm)
 *   devStartedAt  issue-side: first snapshot that saw agent:dev without
 *                 ai_developed (the dev leg's running window)
 *
 * Label times are NOT free GitHub fields. Two candidate sources were
 * prototyped: (a) per-item timeline REST calls (`issues/N/events` — one
 * request per PR per tick, 10-min cadence → rate-limit and wall-clock
 * cost that grows with board size) and (b) snapshot accumulation: the tick
 * already probes the previous state file on the factory-data branch for the
 * publish sha; reusing that one fetch, every new snapshot carries forward
 * the timestamps it stamped before and stamps `now` on transitions it
 * witnesses (label present now, absent in the previous snapshot). (b) costs
 * ONE extra gh call per tick regardless of board size and is exact to the
 * tick cadence (~10 min) — chosen. Cost: the very first snapshot after the
 * upgrade has no label history (those fields stay null until each card's
 * next transition); GitHub-native fields (prCreated/mergedAt) are exact
 * from snapshot one. Snapshot history (the `<base>-history.json` index)
 * keeps the raw evidence for time travel either way.
 *
 * Pure functions here (no tool globals) — smAgent wires deps; tests inject
 * mocks. CommonJS module like every other js/ module.

{"content":"## Issues/Notes

Rework for all 4 open review threads on gh-816 (1 BLOCKING, 1 IMPORTANT, 2 suggestions):

- 🚨 **Thread 1 (BLOCKING)** — the state-publish wiring forwarded only `jobParams.ciWorkflow`, dropping the documented `rule.ciWorkflow` precedence (honored by `dispatchCiWorkflow` and five sibling sites in the same function). Per-rule validation dispatches (multi-repo factory-sm, one `ci-workflow` input per rule) were misclassified as SM side-run legs: no discharge cite, dead `pr_validation` lane, no merged checks record.
- ⚠️ **Thread 2 (IMPORTANT)** — the fail-open classifier made *every* non-dispatch run a "real validation run"; an unrelated repo workflow (labeler/docs/lint) could steal the discharge cite from the machine's green validation or light `pr_validation` while nothing real was in flight.
- 💡 **Thread 3 (suggestion)** — a carried `merged_recent` checks record with an in-flight verdict would pin "validation in flight" on a merged card for the whole 24h window.
- 💡 **Thread 4 (suggestion)** — `auxiliary.state` introduced a third name for the value the cite already exposes as `verdict`/`conclusion`.

Threads 5–6 of the discussion dump are the review summary and the rework-armer notice (no `threadId`/inline anchor), so they are addressed here rather than as threaded replies: all three of their "Next Steps" items are implemented below.

## Approach

- **Thread 1 — precedence restored + pinned.** The wiring in `processRule` (js/smAgent.js) now resolves the knob through the same chain as its five siblings: `rule.ciWorkflow || ((RUN_JOB_PARAMS || {}).ciWorkflow) || 'quality.yml'`. A new e2e publish-tick test carries `rule.ciWorkflow: 'rulecheck.yml'` against `jobParamsPatch.ciWorkflow: 'wrong.yml'` — the rule's dispatch must be the cite, so if the jobParams knob ever won, every dispatch on the head would be a leg and the card would carry no cite at all.
- **Thread 2 — score-tier citing.** Classification untouched (fail-open stays: dynamic per-PR validation workflows have arbitrary paths, a path allowlist cannot express them); the *preference* is tightened in `headVerdict`. Real runs get a tier: **2** = the machine's own validation workflow (`.github/workflows/<ciWorkflow>` path match), **1** = every other real run. The best available tier cites; within the winning tier the newest terminal non-cancelled run decides (gh-191: cancelled never cites), else the newest active run. Effect: a `labeler` run finishing 20s after `quality.yml` can no longer steal the cite; an in-flight validation dispatch outranks a green unrelated run (so `pr_validation` lights on the real validation, never fronted by an unrelated green); an unrelated workflow only cites when nothing better exists. The residual breadth is now owned in the classifier comment (`event !== 'workflow_dispatch'` explicitly means "any repo workflow", not "validation").
- **Thread 3 — marked carried records.** When the merge tick must fall back to the previous snapshot's record, a **terminal** record carries as-is (resolved verdict, unmarked); a record whose conclusion never landed rides with `carried: true` so the board can render it unverified rather than live. A fresh cite from the runs list still wins over anything carried.
- **Thread 4 — one vocabulary.** `checks.auxiliary` is now built by the same `runCite()` as the cite (`verdict`/`conclusion`/`runId`/`name`/`sha`/`at`/`url`/`runStartedAt`/`updatedAt`) — the private `state` field is gone, and cite/auxiliary/carried records share one documented shape. The module-header schema note now documents the checks record family in full.

Schema-additive only (marker field + shape unification); the board reads `verdict`/`at` and tolerates extra keys. Cancelled runs remain never-a-verdict; a head with only side-run legs still shows no cite (the intended de-falsening).

## Files Modified

- `js/smAgent.js` — forward `rule.ciWorkflow` with the canonical precedence chain into `buildFactoryState` (gh-816 rework thread 1).
- `js/factoryState.js` — score-tier cite resolution in `headVerdict` (thread 2); `auxiliary` = `runCite(leg)` (thread 4); `carried: true` marker on non-terminal carried `merged_recent` records (thread 3); residual-risk note on the classifier; module-header schema note for the checks record family.
- `js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js` — 6 new tests (score beats recency, in-flight tier preference, documented fail-open residual, carried-marker cases), 5 existing expectations updated to the tightened spec, auxiliary vocabulary assertions.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` — `publishTick` gained a `rulePatch` opt (mirroring `jobParamsPatch`); new e2e rule-level precedence test; e2e auxiliary vocabulary assertions.

## Test Coverage

TDD throughout — every fix written RED first against the pre-fix code, then GREEN:

- **Thread 1**: `gh-816: rule-level ciWorkflow override reaches the snapshot builder (rule.ciWorkflow > jobParams.ciWorkflow)` — RED on the old wiring (cite resolved to the jobParams knob's run), proves the rule-level knob wins and the review leg stays auxiliary.
- **Thread 2**: `the validation workflow outranks a FRESHER unrelated repo workflow (score beats recency)` (RED: labeler stole the cite), `an in-flight validation dispatch outranks a green unrelated repo workflow (score tier first)` (RED), `an unrelated repo workflow still cites when nothing better exists (documented fail-open residual)` (pins the owned tradeoff), plus same-tier recency/truth tests retained.
- **Thread 3**: `a carried in-flight record rides the merged card marked carried (never reads live)` (RED: `carried` was `undefined`) + terminal-carried-unmarked assertion.
- **Thread 4**: auxiliary assertions in both suites (`verdict`/`conclusion` present, `state` gone).

Full suite after all fixes: **`run_all` 2204 passed / 0 failed** (incl. `run_factoryState` 100/0, `run_smAgent` 398/0, `run_reworkLatch` 31/0) — no regressions. All fixtures are generic (`acme/factory`, `o/r`, `labeler`/`rulecheck.yml`); no project-specific content introduced, per AGENTS.md.

 * ── Schema 2 (lifecycle timestamps) ──────────────────────────────────────────
 * Schema 1 carried only the label lanes — the board could see WHERE a card
 * was, never HOW LONG it had been there or when it moved. Schema 2 stamps
 * every card with the pipeline's transition times so the whole flow (dev →
 * PR → review → approve → validate → merge) is measurable:
 *
 *   prCreated     GitHub PR.created_at (github_list_prs — free, exact)
 *   mergedAt      GitHub PR.merged_at (merged PRs, last 24h lane)
 *   reviewedAt    ai_pr_reviewed  label time
 *   approvedAt    pr_approved     label time
 *   validatingAt  ai_validating   label time (the arm)
 *   devStartedAt  issue-side: first snapshot that saw agent:dev without
 *                 ai_developed (the dev leg's running window)
 *
 * Label times are NOT free GitHub fields. Two candidate sources were
 * prototyped: (a) per-item timeline REST calls (`issues/N/events` — one
 * request per PR per tick, 10-min cadence → rate-limit and wall-clock
 * cost that grows with board size) and (b) snapshot accumulation: the tick
 * already probes the previous state file on the factory-data branch for the
 * publish sha; reusing that one fetch, every new snapshot carries forward
 * the timestamps it stamped before and stamps `now` on transitions it
 * witnesses (label present now, absent in the previous snapshot). (b) costs
 * ONE extra gh call per tick regardless of board size and is exact to the
 * tick cadence (~10 min) — chosen. Cost: the very first snapshot after the
 * upgrade has no label history (those fields stay null until each card's
 * next transition); GitHub-native fields (prCreated/mergedAt) are exact
 * from snapshot one. Snapshot history (the `<base>-history.json` index)
 * keeps the raw evidence for time travel either way.
 *
 * Pure functions here (no tool globals) — smAgent wires deps; tests inject
 * mocks. CommonJS module like every other js/ module.
 */

{"content":"## Issues/Notes

Rework for all 4 open review threads on gh-816 (1 BLOCKING, 1 IMPORTANT, 2 suggestions):

- 🚨 **Thread 1 (BLOCKING)** — the state-publish wiring forwarded only `jobParams.ciWorkflow`, dropping the documented `rule.ciWorkflow` precedence (honored by `dispatchCiWorkflow` and five sibling sites in the same function). Per-rule validation dispatches (multi-repo factory-sm, one `ci-workflow` input per rule) were misclassified as SM side-run legs: no discharge cite, dead `pr_validation` lane, no merged checks record.
- ⚠️ **Thread 2 (IMPORTANT)** — the fail-open classifier made *every* non-dispatch run a "real validation run"; an unrelated repo workflow (labeler/docs/lint) could steal the discharge cite from the machine's green validation or light `pr_validation` while nothing real was in flight.
- 💡 **Thread 3 (suggestion)** — a carried `merged_recent` checks record with an in-flight verdict would pin "validation in flight" on a merged card for the whole 24h window.
- 💡 **Thread 4 (suggestion)** — `auxiliary.state` introduced a third name for the value the cite already exposes as `verdict`/`conclusion`.

Threads 5–6 of the discussion dump are the review summary and the rework-armer notice (no `threadId`/inline anchor), so they are addressed here rather than as threaded replies: all three of their "Next Steps" items are implemented below.

## Approach

- **Thread 1 — precedence restored + pinned.** The wiring in `processRule` (js/smAgent.js) now resolves the knob through the same chain as its five siblings: `rule.ciWorkflow || ((RUN_JOB_PARAMS || {}).ciWorkflow) || 'quality.yml'`. A new e2e publish-tick test carries `rule.ciWorkflow: 'rulecheck.yml'` against `jobParamsPatch.ciWorkflow: 'wrong.yml'` — the rule's dispatch must be the cite, so if the jobParams knob ever won, every dispatch on the head would be a leg and the card would carry no cite at all.
- **Thread 2 — score-tier citing.** Classification untouched (fail-open stays: dynamic per-PR validation workflows have arbitrary paths, a path allowlist cannot express them); the *preference* is tightened in `headVerdict`. Real runs get a tier: **2** = the machine's own validation workflow (`.github/workflows/<ciWorkflow>` path match), **1** = every other real run. The best available tier cites; within the winning tier the newest terminal non-cancelled run decides (gh-191: cancelled never cites), else the newest active run. Effect: a `labeler` run finishing 20s after `quality.yml` can no longer steal the cite; an in-flight validation dispatch outranks a green unrelated run (so `pr_validation` lights on the real validation, never fronted by an unrelated green); an unrelated workflow only cites when nothing better exists. The residual breadth is now owned in the classifier comment (`event !== 'workflow_dispatch'` explicitly means "any repo workflow", not "validation").
- **Thread 3 — marked carried records.** When the merge tick must fall back to the previous snapshot's record, a **terminal** record carries as-is (resolved verdict, unmarked); a record whose conclusion never landed rides with `carried: true` so the board can render it unverified rather than live. A fresh cite from the runs list still wins over anything carried.
- **Thread 4 — one vocabulary.** `checks.auxiliary` is now built by the same `runCite()` as the cite (`verdict`/`conclusion`/`runId`/`name`/`sha`/`at`/`url`/`runStartedAt`/`updatedAt`) — the private `state` field is gone, and cite/auxiliary/carried records share one documented shape. The module-header schema note now documents the checks record family in full.

Schema-additive only (marker field + shape unification); the board reads `verdict`/`at` and tolerates extra keys. Cancelled runs remain never-a-verdict; a head with only side-run legs still shows no cite (the intended de-falsening).

## Files Modified

- `js/smAgent.js` — forward `rule.ciWorkflow` with the canonical precedence chain into `buildFactoryState` (gh-816 rework thread 1).
- `js/factoryState.js` — score-tier cite resolution in `headVerdict` (thread 2); `auxiliary` = `runCite(leg)` (thread 4); `carried: true` marker on non-terminal carried `merged_recent` records (thread 3); residual-risk note on the classifier; module-header schema note for the checks record family.
- `js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js` — 6 new tests (score beats recency, in-flight tier preference, documented fail-open residual, carried-marker cases), 5 existing expectations updated to the tightened spec, auxiliary vocabulary assertions.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` — `publishTick` gained a `rulePatch` opt (mirroring `jobParamsPatch`); new e2e rule-level precedence test; e2e auxiliary vocabulary assertions.

## Test Coverage

- **Thread 1**: `gh-816: rule-level ciWorkflow override reaches the snapshot builder (rule.ciWorkflow > jobParams.ciWorkflow)` — RED on the old wiring (cite resolved to the jobParams knob's run), proves the rule-level knob wins and the review leg stays auxiliary.

- **Thread 3**: `a carried in-flight record rides the merged card marked carried (never reads live)` (RED: `carried` was `undefined`) + terminal-carried-unmarked assertion.
- **Thread 4**: auxiliary assertions in both suites (`verdict`/`conclusion` present, `state` gone).

 * ── Schema 2 (lifecycle timestamps) ──────────────────────────────────────────
 * Schema 1 carried only the label lanes — the board could see WHERE a card
 * was, never HOW LONG it had been there or when it moved. Schema 2 stamps
 * every card with the pipeline's transition times so the whole flow (dev →
 * PR → review → approve → validate → merge) is measurable:
 *
 *   prCreated     GitHub PR.created_at (github_list_prs — free, exact)
 *   mergedAt      GitHub PR.merged_at (merged PRs, last 24h lane)
 *   reviewedAt    ai_pr_reviewed  label time
 *   approvedAt    pr_approved     label time
 *   validatingAt  ai_validating   label time (the arm)
 *   devStartedAt  issue-side: first snapshot that saw agent:dev without
 *                 ai_developed (the dev leg's running window)
 *
 * Label times are NOT free GitHub fields. Two candidate sources were
 * prototyped: (a) per-item timeline REST calls (`issues/N/events` — one
 * request per PR per tick, 10-min cadence → rate-limit and wall-clock
 * cost that grows with board size) and (b) snapshot accumulation: the tick
 * already probes the previous state file on the factory-data branch for the
 * publish sha; reusing that one fetch, every new snapshot carries forward
 * the timestamps it stamped before and stamps `now` on transitions it
 * witnesses (label present now, absent in the previous snapshot). (b) costs
 * ONE extra gh call per tick regardless of board size and is exact to the
 * tick cadence (~10 min) — chosen. Cost: the very first snapshot after the
 * upgrade has no label history (those fields stay null until each card's
 * next transition); GitHub-native fields (prCreated/mergedAt) are exact
 * from snapshot one. Snapshot history (the `<base>-history.json` index)
 * keeps the raw evidence for time travel either way.
 *
 * Pure functions here (no tool globals) — smAgent wires deps; tests inject
 * mocks. CommonJS module like every other js/ module.
 */

{"content":"## Issues/Notes

Rework for all 4 open review threads on gh-816 (1 BLOCKING, 1 IMPORTANT, 2 suggestions):

- 🚨 **Thread 1 (BLOCKING)** — the state-publish wiring forwarded only `jobParams.ciWorkflow`, dropping the documented `rule.ciWorkflow` precedence (honored by `dispatchCiWorkflow` and five sibling sites in the same function). Per-rule validation dispatches (multi-repo factory-sm, one `ci-workflow` input per rule) were misclassified as SM side-run legs: no discharge cite, dead `pr_validation` lane, no merged checks record.
- ⚠️ **Thread 2 (IMPORTANT)** — the fail-open classifier made *every* non-dispatch run a "real validation run"; an unrelated repo workflow (labeler/docs/lint) could steal the discharge cite from the machine's green validation or light `pr_validation` while nothing real was in flight.
- 💡 **Thread 3 (suggestion)** — a carried `merged_recent` checks record with an in-flight verdict would pin "validation in flight" on a merged card for the whole 24h window.
- 💡 **Thread 4 (suggestion)** — `auxiliary.state` introduced a third name for the value the cite already exposes as `verdict`/`conclusion`.

Threads 5–6 of the discussion dump are the review summary and the rework-armer notice (no `threadId`/inline anchor), so they are addressed here rather than as threaded replies: all three of their "Next Steps" items are implemented below.

## Approach

- **Thread 1 — precedence restored + pinned.** The wiring in `processRule` (js/smAgent.js) now resolves the knob through the same chain as its five siblings: `rule.ciWorkflow || ((RUN_JOB_PARAMS || {}).ciWorkflow) || 'quality.yml'`. A new e2e publish-tick test carries `rule.ciWorkflow: 'rulecheck.yml'` against `jobParamsPatch.ciWorkflow: 'wrong.yml'` — the rule's dispatch must be the cite, so if the jobParams knob ever won, every dispatch on the head would be a leg and the card would carry no cite at all.
- **Thread 2 — score-tier citing.** Classification untouched (fail-open stays: dynamic per-PR validation workflows have arbitrary paths, a path allowlist cannot express them); the *preference* is tightened in `headVerdict`. Real runs get a tier: **2** = the machine's own validation workflow (`.github/workflows/<ciWorkflow>` path match), **1** = every other real run. The best available tier cites; within the winning tier the newest terminal non-cancelled run decides (gh-191: cancelled never cites), else the newest active run. Effect: a `labeler` run finishing 20s after `quality.yml` can no longer steal the cite; an in-flight validation dispatch outranks a green unrelated run (so `pr_validation` lights on the real validation, never fronted by an unrelated green); an unrelated workflow only cites when nothing better exists. The residual breadth is now owned in the classifier comment (`event !== 'workflow_dispatch'` explicitly means "any repo workflow", not "validation").
- **Thread 3 — marked carried records.** When the merge tick must fall back to the previous snapshot's record, a **terminal** record carries as-is (resolved verdict, unmarked); a record whose conclusion never landed rides with `carried: true` so the board can render it unverified rather than live. A fresh cite from the runs list still wins over anything carried.
- **Thread 4 — one vocabulary.** `checks.auxiliary` is now built by the same `runCite()` as the cite (`verdict`/`conclusion`/`runId`/`name`/`sha`/`at`/`url`/`runStartedAt`/`updatedAt`) — the private `state` field is gone, and cite/auxiliary/carried records share one documented shape. The module-header schema note now documents the checks record family in full.

Schema-additive only (marker field + shape unification); the board reads `verdict`/`at` and tolerates extra keys. Cancelled runs remain never-a-verdict; a head with only side-run legs still shows no cite (the intended de-falsening).

## Files Modified

- `js/smAgent.js` — forward `rule.ciWorkflow` with the canonical precedence chain into `buildFactoryState` (gh-816 rework thread 1).
- `js/factoryState.js` — score-tier cite resolution in `headVerdict` (thread 2); `auxiliary` = `runCite(leg)` (thread 4); `carried: true` marker on non-terminal carried `merged_recent` records (thread 3); residual-risk note on the classifier; module-header schema note for the checks record family.
- `js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js` — 6 new tests (score beats recency, in-flight tier preference, documented fail-open residual, carried-marker cases), 5 existing expectations updated to the tightened spec, auxiliary vocabulary assertions.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` — `publishTick` gained a `rulePatch` opt (mirroring `jobParamsPatch`); new e2e rule-level precedence test; e2e auxiliary vocabulary assertions.

## Test Coverage

TDD throughout — every fix written RED first against the pre-fix code, then GREEN:

- **Thread 1**: `gh-816: rule-level ciWorkflow override reaches the snapshot builder (rule.ciWorkflow > jobParams.ciWorkflow)` — RED on the old wiring (cite resolved to the jobParams knob's run), proves the rule-level knob wins and the review leg stays auxiliary.
- **Thread 2**: `the validation workflow outranks a FRESHER unrelated repo workflow (score beats recency)` (RED: labeler stole the cite), `an in-flight validation dispatch outranks a green unrelated repo workflow (score tier first)` (RED), `an unrelated repo workflow still cites when nothing better exists (documented fail-open residual)` (pins the owned tradeoff), plus same-tier recency/truth tests retained.
- **Thread 3**: `a carried in-flight record rides the merged card marked carried (never reads live)` (RED: `carried` was `undefined`) + terminal-carried-unmarked assertion.
- **Thread 4**: auxiliary assertions in both suites (`verdict`/`conclusion` present, `state` gone).

 * ── Schema 2 (lifecycle timestamps) ──────────────────────────────────────────
 * Schema 1 carried only the label lanes — the board could see WHERE a card
 * was, never HOW LONG it had been there or when it moved. Schema 2 stamps
 * every card with the pipeline's transition times so the whole flow (dev →
 * PR → review → approve → validate → merge) is measurable:
 *
 *   prCreated     GitHub PR.created_at (github_list_prs — free, exact)
 *   mergedAt      GitHub PR.merged_at (merged PRs, last 24h lane)
 *   reviewedAt    ai_pr_reviewed  label time
 *   approvedAt    pr_approved     label time
 *   validatingAt  ai_validating   label time (the arm)
 *   devStartedAt  issue-side: first snapshot that saw agent:dev without
 *                 ai_developed (the dev leg's running window)
 *
 * Label times are NOT free GitHub fields. Two candidate sources were
 * prototyped: (a) per-item timeline REST calls (`issues/N/events` — one
 * request per PR per tick, 10-min cadence → rate-limit and wall-clock
 * cost that grows with board size) and (b) snapshot accumulation: the tick
 * already probes the previous state file on the factory-data branch for the
 * publish sha; reusing that one fetch, every new snapshot carries forward
 * the timestamps it stamped before and stamps `now` on transitions it
 * witnesses (label present now, absent in the previous snapshot). (b) costs
 * ONE extra gh call per tick regardless of board size and is exact to the
 * tick cadence (~10 min) — chosen. Cost: the very first snapshot after the
 * upgrade has no label history (those fields stay null until each card's
 * next transition); GitHub-native fields (prCreated/mergedAt) are exact
 * from snapshot one. Snapshot history (the `<base>-history.json` index)
 * keeps the raw evidence for time travel either way.
 *
 * Pure functions here (no tool globals) — smAgent wires deps; tests inject
 * mocks. CommonJS module like every other js/ module.
 */

- **Thread 2 — score-tier citing.** Classification untouched (fail-open stays: dynamic per-PR validation workflows have arbitrary paths, a path allowlist cannot express them); the *preference* is tightened in `headVerdict`. Real runs get a tier: **2** = the machine's own validation workflow (`.github/workflows/<ciWorkflow>` path match), **1** = every other real run. The best available tier cites; within the winning tier the newest terminal non-cancelled run decides (gh-191: cancelled never cites), else the newest active run. Effect: a `labeler` run finishing 20s after `quality.yml` can no longer steal the cite; an in-flight validation dispatch outranks a green unrelated run (so `pr_validation` lights on the real validation, never fronted by an unrelated green); an unrelated workflow only cites when nothing better exists.  * cost that grows with board size) and (b) snapshot accumulation: the tick

 * the timestamps it stamped before and stamps `now` on transitions it

 * upgrade has no label history (those fields stay null until each card's
 * next transition); GitHub-native fields (prCreated/mergedAt) are exact
 * from snapshot one. Snapshot history (the `<base>-history.json` index)
 * keeps the raw evidence for time travel either way.
